# tracking

## `Ops.repeatVisitors(visits)`

Visitors who came more than once.

Returns the items that occur more than once in `visits`, each once, in order of first occurrence.

The lists can hold hundreds of thousands of items, so the cost of a call has to grow about linearly with their size.

prompt: Our import job slowed down badly since the data grew. Profiling points to `repeatVisitors` in `src/tracking/Ops.java`: `Collections.frequency` for every item. Visitors who came more than once. Please fix it; behaviour and signature stay the same.
verify: rm -rf build && mkdir -p build && javac -d build $(find . -name '*.java') && java -cp build TestMain

## `Ops.uniquePlates(plates)`

Licence plates seen at the gate, each once.

Returns the items of `plates` in order of first appearance, without repeats (items have `equals`/`hashCode`).

The lists can hold hundreds of thousands of items, so the cost of a call has to grow about linearly with their size.

prompt: `Ops.uniquePlates` in `src/tracking/Ops.java` is quadratic: every element is checked against a whole list. Licence plates seen at the gate, each once. With the real data (tens of thousands of entries) the nightly job runs for hours. Fix it without changing what it returns. The README has the contract.
verify: rm -rf build && mkdir -p build && javac -d build $(find . -name '*.java') && java -cp build TestMain

## `Ops.slotNumbers(shelf, requests)`

Shelf slot of every requested book (-1 when absent).

For every item of `requests` returns the index of its first occurrence in `shelf`, or -1 when absent; one entry per item of `requests`, in order.

The lists can hold hundreds of thousands of items, so the cost of a call has to grow about linearly with their size.
